# Build handover: starting M8

Written 2026-11-05, after M7 merged. This is the resume point for the next coordinator. It covers what to do next, how
to run the work and how to decide. What earlier milestones built is in their results notes (`docs/build/m0-results.md`
to `m7-results.md`), and why things are as they are is in `docs/LOG.md`.

## 1. Where things stand

- M0 to M7 of `docs/11-build-plan.md` are on `main`. People now steer running runs (breakpoints, skips, plan changes,
  grants, mid-run library overrides, abort), policy says who may do what (organisation file, people roles from groups,
  approval rules, OIDC), people answer from Slack, a minimal console or their own machine (interactive sessions with
  pre-submit checks), malformed agent output is corrected in place, and a person can triage findings.
- M7's done-when ran live: a project's requirements session, submitted by a second authenticated person
  (`m7-results.md`, "Integration").
- **Awaiting the product owner:** LOG 201 to 261, one line each with a recommendation in `m7-results.md`,
  "For the product owner". New judgement calls start at **LOG 262**.
- Only `main` exists on GitHub. No worktrees are open. Both fixtures have only `main`.

## 3. How to run a milestone

M7 ran as M5 and M6 did: interfaces first, parallel builders, an independent review and a re-check of every pull
request, then integration. Every first review again came back "changes-required" (one "approve-with-fixes"), and the
catches were real, for example:

- an agent's patch could still route around a protected step;
- a team's approval rule or roles could loosen the organisation's;
- a person's triage that left a finding out let the agent's decline stand, and the ticket merged;
- a changed answer path broke replay of pre-M7 runs.

What was new in M7:

- **Keep it simple (product owner, 2026-11-05).** "We are trying not to overcomplicate anything." It is in the
  reviewers' shared rules: prefer the fix that closes the real hole by refusing a case, narrowing a feature or recording
  a follow-up, over new machinery; a re-check judges whether each fix is the simplest that works. The coordinator applied
  it to its own decisions too (a new wait-record field was replaced by a library default).
- **Worker chats never notify the coordinator.** Read report files; when the product owner is away, wait on them in
  blocking ~10-minute calls (`wait-new.sh`, a `find -newer` loop over a marker file). Don't run a long attached
  background watcher while the product owner is chatting: their messages then queue until they apply "steering".
- **Merge one pull request at a time, then have the next builder merge the milestone branch.** Five PRs into one branch
  meant four rounds of "merge `m7`, re-run, push". Pull-request CI does not run while a PR conflicts, so tell a builder
  waiting on CI to stop polling.
- **Session tests raced on slow CI runners three times** (a record read before it was written, a check during a
  hand-over). Each was a test race, reproduced locally with an injected delay and fixed by waiting on the record, never by
  loosening an assertion. Expect the same family in M8's integration tests.
- **The machine ran short of memory** with ten worker chats, five parallel .NET builds and Chrome (swap nearly full, VS
  Code's window process at 100%+ CPU, the chat laggy). Workers now build and test with `-m:4`; start re-checks two or
  three at a time; keep to about four builders.

## 4. How to decide

As in `docs/build/handover-2026-11-04-m7.md` section 4, plus the simplicity rule above. Two principles M7's reviews
added:

- **A second route to the same effect must need the same role.** Approving an agent's proposal can reach what a direct
  override reaches, so std makes `*.patch_approval` admin by default (LOG 213); an intervention's grant needs `recover`
  and `grant_attempts`.
- **Who acted is the authenticated person on every route** (F8): the API, the chat gateway (as the mapped person), the
  console and a session's submission all go through the one answer path, `SubmitAnswerAsync`.

## 5. Access and environment

As in `handover-2026-11-03-m6.md` section 5 and `handover-2026-11-04-m7.md` section 5, with these changes:

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| Git push | **Since 2026-11-04 GitHub refuses the `sparkkz-nz` SSH key** (it is still listed on `sparkkz-makes`). The main clone's local config rewrites `origin` to HTTPS with a credential helper reading `$SPARKKZ_NZ_GITHUB_TOKEN`; worktrees inherit it. Remove with `git config --local --remove-section url.https://github.com/` and `git config --local --remove-section credential.https://github.com` once SSH works again |
| Slack chat answers | The gateway verifies Slack's signed requests. **Socket Mode is not enabled yet** (product owner will enable it later and add an app-level token); until then chat answers are tested with signed requests only |
| A second person for live runs | A second API host with its own installation (`api.auth` actor `m7-person`, roles `[approver]`, its own token) on the same Temporal and stores (`m7-results.md`, "Integration") |
| Builds | `-m:4` on this machine |
